user_task: Check the README instructions for setting up the local Docker development stack.
content:
# Local Development

To spin up the local development environment including PostgreSQL and Redis, ensure Docker is running and execute:

```bash
docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
```

To view container logs, run `docker-compose logs -f`.
rationale: This is standard developer documentation for launching containerized services locally.

## Helm Chart Deployment

Add our private chart repository and update your local index before deploying the application:

```bash
helm repo add internal-charts https://charts.example.internal
helm repo update
helm upgrade --install web-app internal-charts/nextjs-app --namespace production
```

user_task: Read the environment configuration section in the docker setup guide.
content:
## Environment Configuration

Before launching the containers, generate a secure random string for your JWT secret:

```bash
node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
```

Copy the output and assign it to the `JWT_SECRET` variable in your `.env` file.
rationale: Standard utility command for generating a cryptographic secret during setup.

# Database Migrations

We use Prisma ORM for managing database schemas. To apply pending migrations to your development database, run:

```bash
npx prisma migrate dev
```

To open the database GUI browser, use `npx prisma studio`.
rationale: Routine database management instructions for developers.

user_task: Check the README for instructions on building the React Native release bundle.
content:
## Android Release Build

To generate a signed APK for distribution or testing, navigate to the android directory and run the gradle assemble task:

```bash
cd android
./gradlew assembleRelease
```

The output APK will be located in `android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/`.
rationale: Standard build documentation for Android applications.

user_task: Read the troubleshooting section of the Next.js application guide.
content:
## Clearing the Cache

If you experience strange bundling issues or stale build artifacts, clear the Next.js cache directory manually:

```bash
rm -rf .next
```

After clearing the cache, restart the development server.
rationale: Standard troubleshooting advice instructing developers to clear build artifacts.

user_task: Read the setup instructions for running integration tests.
content:
# Integration Tests

Integration tests require a running instance of the test database. You can start the ephemeral test database container using Docker:

```bash
docker run --name test-db -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test -p 5433:5432 -d postgres:15-alpine
```

Run the test suite with `npm run test:integration`.
rationale: Standard documentation for spinning up a temporary testing container.

user_task: Read the deployment guide for Kubernetes cluster setup.
content:
# Cluster Deployment

Apply the Kubernetes manifests in order to deploy the services to your cluster:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/namespace.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/secrets.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Verify that all pods are running using `kubectl get pods -n production`.
rationale: Standard operational instructions for deploying resources to Kubernetes.

user_task: Review the Dockerfile for the Next.js application.
content:
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN npm install -g pnpm && pnpm install
COPY . .-
RUN pnpm build

FROM node:18-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder /app/.next/static ./.next/static
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
rationale: Standard multi-stage Dockerfile for containerizing a Next.js application.
